title: Smooth seasonal phases and trend
summary: STL alternates local seasonal and trend smoothing while retaining a residual component.

steps.title: Form seasonal-phase subseries
steps.text: After removing the current trend, collect values at the same phase in successive cycles. STL smooths along each of these subseries, allowing the seasonal pattern to vary through the record.

steps.title: Use local polynomial smoothing
steps.text: The illustrative panel computes a tricube-weighted local linear fit for one phase. Full STL also extends boundaries, applies low-pass filtering, and combines the smoothed subseries; the illustration is not a replacement implementation of those internals.

steps.title: Alternate seasonal and trend
steps.text: The seasonal estimate is subtracted to form a deseasonalized series, which is smoothed for trend. The numerical checkpoints come from exact statsmodels fits with one through five inner iterations and no outer robustness loop.

steps.title: Form the additive result
steps.text: The final five-iteration checkpoint matches the configured DeTime STL wrapper. Residual is the input minus the returned trend and seasonal component. Reconstruction consistency does not validate a unique physical interpretation.

parameters.name: period
parameters.effect: Specified number of samples in a seasonal cycle; this example uses 12.

parameters.name: seasonal
parameters.effect: Odd LOESS span across cycles for the seasonal subseries; smaller spans allow faster seasonal change.

parameters.name: trend / low_pass
parameters.effect: Odd smoothing spans controlling trend and low-pass behavior; this example uses 23 and 13.

parameters.name: robust
parameters.effect: Controls the outer reweighting loop. ROBUST_STL defaults to True; setting it False disables robustness.

cautions: ROBUST_STL is the registry name for statsmodels STL with its robust option. This name does not establish implementation of other published algorithms also called RobustSTL.
Smoothing spans, seasonal period, endpoint handling, and outliers influence the estimated components.
The animation uses statsmodels' actual checkpoints. Internal fits are restarted for each budget; frame count is not an execution-time measure.
STL is an offline smoother. Use only available history when constructing forecasting features.

references.title: Cleveland et al. (1990), STL: A Seasonal-Trend Decomposition Procedure Based on Loess
statsmodels STL: parameters and implementation contract

trace_note: The local weighted regression illustrates LOESS numerically and omits STL's full low-pass and boundary machinery. Exact statsmodels inner-iteration checkpoints and final DeTime output are shown separately and compared.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
